I work in Mandarin and English, and I maintain LazyEdit, a local-first workflow for transcription, subtitle timing, multilingual captions, short vertical renders, and reviewed publishing. Two relevant project-owned examples are a 23-second 9:16 timed-text piece (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=G9NKncZgRis) and a 30-second scene with 15 aligned segments and subtitle exports (https://lachlanchen.github.io/LalaMedias/videos/aginti-autonomous-lab-ai-glasses-2b85b0d9.html). I have also prepared an attached 19-second English/Traditional Chinese sample using first-party L-and-N app screens and audio. For a paid trial, I can return one polished 15–60 second master, two hook variations, burned captions plus SRT, and export notes for the requested formats. For Taiwan, I would confirm the audience, Traditional Chinese wording, CTA, brand constraints, and one conversion goal before editing rather than mechanically translating the captions. My public examples are workflow pieces rather than customer ads, so your paid trial is the right fit test; I won't claim ROAS or cost-per-lead figures I don't have. I can begin at USD 18/hour.

practical_guide.content:
A lecture can have accurate words and still make a poor study resource if its transcript, translation, subtitles, and notes each become a separate copy.

A safer workflow is to correct the timed source once, preserve stable segment IDs, derive the subtitle and pocket-book formats from it, then test a translated term by seeking back to the exact second.

I wrote out the full method with a small, working three-language example:
https://blog.lazying.art/html/computer_internet/3792/turn-lecture-into-bilingual-subtitles-study-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=bilingual_lecture_pack_pilot&utm_content=source_first_guide
